title: Regular-file partial-progress EINTR restart candidate
mechanism: Candidate: sys_read/sys_write map any backend EINTR to ERESTARTSYS without a progress count, so an SA_RESTART replay could repeat a committed partial transfer. Rejected because no regular-file backend returns EINTR (waits are uninterruptible and copy faults are EFAULT).
contract: signal(7): regular-file (disk) I/O is not interrupted by signals. Read(2)/write(2) return a partial count when interrupted after transferring data.
observed: Under roughly 17k to 45k signals per section, regular-file read/write on ramfs and ext2 (buffered, O_DIRECT, O_SYNC) never returned EINTR, and O_APPEND size and shared offset equalled the sum of returned counts, matching Linux. The pipe control restarted as expected.

repro.how_to_run: Negative probe: run the binary with --ctrl, then with <dir> <label> [direct|sync] on /tmp and /ext2 in the guest and on a Linux host. UNINTERRUPTIBLE, NO_REPLAY and NO_DOUBLE_ADVANCE confirm the false positive, and the pipe control must print RESTARTED.
repro.runtime_status: negative probe ran at 604948581 (01a CR-1, SMP=2): no regular-file EINTR, no replay. FALSE POSITIVE

caveats: Regular files only. Pipes are AST-09 (reproduced) and sockets remain AST-39. The rejection depends on no backend returning EINTR after committed progress. matches.json classifies it NON_ACTIONABLE_RECORD. #3576 rewrites the same lines but is a different defect.
